 Go confident of hitting targets despite shake-up in BOC, BIR
 By Niña Myka Pauline Arceo
 November 17, 2026
 10
 Resize 
 Small 
 Medium 
 Large 
 THE government remains optimistic about meeting its revenue collection targets this year despite leadership changes at its two main tax agencies, Finance Secretary Frederick Go said.
 “I’m very confident about the leadership in both the Bureau of Customs and Bureau of Internal Revenue,” Go told reporters at the sidelines of the Asean Summit on Saturday.
 Commissioner Charlito Martin Mendoza, who previously headed the BIR, has moved to the BOC, while former Finance Undersecretary Rolando Ligon has taken over as the new BIR commissioner.
 Go said both agencies would continue implementing the programs introduced under Mendoza and former Customs commissioner and now Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) President and CEO Ariel Nepomuceno, ensuring that the leadership transition would not disrupt the agency’s operations.He expressed confidence that Ligon and Mendoza would sustain the initiatives of their predecessor.
 “We’ll have continuity and no disruption,” Go said.

 The BIR has a collection target of P3.39 trillion this year, while the Customs is expected to collect P1.011 trillion.
 Go was particularly optimistic about Custom’s ability to achieve its annual collection goal, citing the seasonal increase in revenue typically recorded during the fourth quarter.
 Advertisement 
 “We will continue to experience the seasonal high of the Bureau of Customs in the fourth quarter,” Go said.
 As of October, Customs recorded its highest monthly collection, reaching P97.463 billion from P82.962 billion collected in October 2025. It also reached 99.42 percent of the month’s P98.028 billion revenue target.
 “I’m very confident that BOC will hit the targets and now with Charlie Mendoza there, Charlie is very good at reforms. I must say, the reforms he instituted at the BIR were very challenging [but] he was able to do it,” Go added.
 For the BIR, however, Go acknowledged that revenue performance would remain closely tied to the country’s economic growth. 
 Advertisement 
 “So I think that’s the better metric to evaluate the BIR’s performance, and I believe that now Commissioner John Ligon will continue with all the programs of then-commissioner Charlie Mendoza,” Go said.
 Mendoza previously said they are targeting to surpass P3 trillion in gross revenue collections before the end of November, after their collections reached P2.81 trillion in the first 10 months of 2026.
 Data from the bureau showed that collections in the January to October period reached P2.81 trillion, up 5.63 percent from the P2.66 trillion recorded in the same period last year.
 For October alone, the bureau collected P348.54 billion, up 5.92 percent or P19.48 billion from the P329.06 billion recorded in October last year.
